title: The First Bug
text: In 1947, engineers working on an early computer at Harvard traced a fault to a moth stuck inside a relay. They taped the insect into their logbook and wrote, "First actual case of bug being found." The word bug was already used for glitches, but the story made it famous.

title: How a Message Travels
text: When you send a message online, it is chopped into small packets. Each packet may take a different route across the network, hopping between routers like a letter passing through post offices. At the other end, the packets are put back in order. If one goes missing, the receiving computer simply asks for it again.

title: Long Beats Complex
text: A long password made of several unrelated words is usually stronger than a short one filled with symbols. Computers guessing passwords care about how many possibilities exist, and every extra character multiplies that number. A phrase that is easy for you to remember can be very hard for a machine to guess.

title: Code: Greeting Function
text: const greet = (name) => { if (!name) { return "Hello, stranger!"; } return `Hello, ${name}!`; }; console.log(greet("Ada")); console.log(greet());

title: Code: Fibonacci
text: def fib(n): a, b = 0, 1 for _ in range(n): yield a a, b = b, a + b print(list(fib(10)))

title: Counting in Twos
text: Computers count with only two digits, zero and one, because a switch is either off or on. A single digit is called a bit, and eight bits make a byte. With just one byte, a computer can write any number from zero to two hundred fifty-five.
